## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Sīlavīmaṁsakajātaka* (Ja 290), rendered in English as *A Test of Virtue*, belongs to the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. According to the framing narrative preserved in the tradition, the story opens with the verse motto “Virtue is lovely” and was delivered by the Buddha at Jetavana [SuttaCentral]. It concerns a brahmin who put his own reputation to the test, sharing its origin story and narrative circumstances with the *Sīlavīmaṁsa* tale found in the first book of the Jātaka [SuttaCentral]. In a study of Buddhist narrative nomenclature, J. S. Speyer notes that the title *Sīlavīmaṁsa(ka)-Jātaka* provides a prime example of traditional birth-story headings where the initial component of the compound designates an action rather than a Bodhisattva or an object [Speyer 1895]. A related title, *Sīlavīmaṁsaka-jātaka*, is also cataloged by Bhikkhu Nyanatusita among Southeast Asian non-canonical Jātaka traditions [Nyanatusita 2008].

SuttaCentral records four translations of the text in four modern languages [SuttaCentral]. Text-reuse analysis conducted by DharmaNexus indicates no cross-language matches in Sanskrit, Chinese, or Tibetan corpora with a score of 10 or above [DharmaNexus]. Within Pali literature, DharmaNexus records three matching passages comprising 594 characters shared with the commentary in the *Jātaka-aṭṭhakathā* (*Dutiyo bhāgo*), with the longest continuous correspondence spanning segments §0.4–3.4 and commentary units §2773–2780 at a 0.93 similarity score [DharmaNexus].
